title: Fluted Floating Shelves: Sizes, Finishes and Prices
meta_description: Fluted floating shelves start at $469.00. Measure your wall, choose width, depth and wood finish, and see when a custom size or hand-carving is worth it.
body_html:
A fluted floating shelf from Wrydeco starts at $469.00. Which one suits you depends on three things: how wide your wall is, how deep the objects you'll display are, and which wood tone works against the rest of the room. Each section below turns one of those into a measurement you can take today.

In this guide

  1. What are fluted shelves, and is fluting the style you want?
  2. What size fluted floating shelf do you need?
  3. Which wood finish should you choose?
  4. When is a custom size or hand-carving worth paying for?
  5. Worked example: planning a fluted shelf for one wall

What are fluted shelves, and is fluting the style you want?

A fluted shelf has parallel grooves cut along its face. The grooves catch light and show texture even when the shelf is empty. Wrydeco's fluted design is the Handmade Fluted Wood Floating Shelf, which also has a scalloped edge. It sits in a collection of 16 floating wood shelves priced from $469.00 to $2658.00, and the other styles look very different. If you're not set on fluting yet, you can compare all 16 floating wood shelves side by side.

How to apply it: stand where you'll see the wall most often and look at the furniture already there. If the room is mostly straight lines, a fluted shelf adds texture without fighting them. If it already has a lot of pattern, a plain bowl shape may sit more quietly.

What to check

  • Does the room already have strong pattern (rugs, tiles, wallpaper) that fluting would compete with?
  • Is this shelf for display, storage or both?
  • Does the starting price for your style fit your budget before you add size or finish options?

What size fluted floating shelf do you need?

The collection lists these standard sizes at the slim end of the range:

  • Width: 24"W x 3.5"H, 32"W x 3.5"H, 48"W x 3.5"H
  • Depth: 5"D or 7"D
  • Starting price: the 24"W x 3.5"H width and the 5"D depth each start at $469.00

The 3.5" figure is the shelf's height, meaning how thick it looks from the front. It's the same at every width, so the choice comes down to width and depth. Check the listing directly to see which specific wood tones and custom carving choices apply to this fluted profile.

[IMAGE: wrydeco_logo_39305901834330.jpg]

How to apply it: measure the clear width of the wall where the shelf will go, from corner to corner or between window frames. Then mark 24", 32" and 48" on the wall with painter's tape and step back. A shelf that nearly fills an alcove looks deliberate. One that stops well short can look like the wrong size. For depth, measure the deepest object you plan to put on the shelf. If it's more than 5" deep, it will hang over a 5"D shelf.

For mounting, solid wood floating shelves should be anchored directly into wall studs to achieve maximum weight capacity, especially if you plan to display heavier ceramic or stone decor.

What to check

  • Clear wall width, measured at the height you'll mount the shelf
  • Depth of the deepest object you'll display
  • What's behind the wall where you'll fix the shelf
  • Whether the shelf needs to clear a light switch, outlet or door swing

Which wood finish should you choose?

These finishes appear across the floating wood shelves collection:

  • Natural
  • Natural Finish
  • Light Oak
  • Walnut
  • Dark Walnut
  • Warm Wood
  • Dark Warm Wood
  • Cool Dark Wood
  • Custom

They're not all offered on the same shelf at the same price. Warm Wood, Dark Warm Wood, Cool Dark Wood, Natural Finish, Dark Walnut and Custom each start at $469.00. Natural, Light Oak and Walnut each start at $576.90. The product page for each shelf shows which of these you can pick on it.

How to apply it: start with the undertone. Warm Wood and Dark Warm Wood lean toward the reds and oranges of most hardwood floors and older furniture. Cool Dark Wood suits grey, black or white rooms. Then look at the wood already in the room. Matching it closely makes the shelf blend in. A clearly lighter or darker finish makes the shelf stand out as its own piece. Fluting cuts small shadows into the face, so judge the finish in the light the shelf will actually get, not just in a product photo.

What to check

  • Is the floor or main furniture warm-toned or cool-toned?
  • Should the shelf match the existing wood or contrast with it?
  • Is the finish you want offered on the fluted shelf itself?
  • If you're choosing between "Natural" and "Natural Finish", how do they compare side by side on the product page?

When is a custom size or hand-carving worth paying for?

One listing in the collection offers these options:

Do you need a custom size?

  • No
  • Yes, smaller
  • Yes, a bit larger (no more than 5")
  • Other: contact Wrydeco before ordering

Would you like to hand-carve text or art?

  • No
  • Yes, custom name/text
  • Yes, image/pattern
  • Yes, engrave text and image

On that listing, these are the starting prices:

  • No custom size: $576.90
  • Smaller: $576.90
  • A bit larger: $696.90
  • Custom name/text: $626.90
  • Image/pattern: $776.90

A smaller size starts at the same price as no custom size. Going larger or adding carving each starts higher.

How to apply it: a custom size makes sense when your wall falls between two standard widths and the gap matters to you. If you need more than 5" beyond a standard size, the listing asks you to contact Wrydeco before ordering. Carving is worth it when the shelf marks something specific, like a family name in an entryway. On a fluted face, ask how carving would sit alongside the grooves before you order.

What to check

  • How far is your measured width from the nearest standard width?
  • Is the difference within 5", or do you need to contact Wrydeco first?
  • Does the fluted shelf's own product page offer custom sizing and carving?

Worked example: planning a fluted shelf for one wall

All measurements in this example are hypothetical. They're chosen to fall between the listed sizes so the decision has to be made.

Picture an alcove above a dark sideboard. It's wider than 32" but narrower than 48". The plan is to display a few ceramics, and the deepest piece, a vase, is more than 5" across but less than 7".

  1. Width. A 48"W shelf won't fit. A 32"W shelf fits and leaves some wall on each side. Measure that leftover. If the shelf would look short and the extra width you want is within the "a bit larger (no more than 5\")" option, ask about it. If you need more than that, contact Wrydeco or stay with a centred 32"W.
  2. Depth. The vase would overhang a 5"D shelf, so 7"D is the safer choice.
  3. Finish. The sideboard is dark and the floor is warm-toned, which points to Dark Walnut or Dark Warm Wood rather than Cool Dark Wood. Both start at $469.00 in the collection's finish list.
  4. Carving. It's a display shelf, not a name sign, so no carving.
  5. Cost. The 24"W x 3.5"H width and the 5"D depth each start at $469.00. Choosing a wider 32" span or a deeper 7" profile will adjust the total price based on wood volume, which updates automatically as you select your options on the product page.

With your own width, deepest object and finish worked out, you can choose your width, depth and finish on the fluted shelf.
